# LaunchDarkly migration & GrowthBook experience - 1-800-Flowers
Date: 2026-08-19 | Duration: 42m

## Summary
The meeting highlighted the successful migration from LaunchDarkly to GrowthBook, achieving 95% completion by late July. Joseph Treman emphasized challenges with feature flag functionality, noting GrowthBook's limitations on storing unused flag variations which required workflow adjustments. The integration of custom metrics pipelines was a core advantage, enhancing existing tracking systems. Future usage aims to empower non-technical stakeholders while maintaining control in experimentation workflows. However, data consistency issues in product analytics pose barriers to broad rollout until resolved. Ongoing collaboration with GrowthBook is essential for roadmap clarity and maximizing platform utilization, showcasing the need for deeper integration and feedback mechanisms.

## Keywords
Migration, Feature Flagging, Experimentation, Metrics Control, Iterative Testing, Product Analytics

# LaunchDarkly migration & GrowthBook experience - Upstart
Date: 2026-08-20 | Duration: 39m

## Summary
The discussion centered on the complexities and challenges faced during the migration from LaunchDarkly to Growth Book, which took about a year. Key issues included the choice of cleaning legacy feature flags versus carrying them forward, leading to a split approach that increased technical debt. User experience differences created a learning curve, as engineers struggled to adapt when shifting from one platform to another. The switch was primarily driven by cost considerations and the capabilities of Growth Book, including self-hosting options that better aligned with data control needs. Furthermore, there are ongoing efforts to enhance the experimentation culture, which involve forming a dedicated team and addressing data quality for experiment analysis. Future plans include utilizing AI tools for improved experiment design and ongoing training resources to support teams.

## Keywords
Growth Book, LaunchDarkly migration, experimentation platform, feature flags, stale flag cleanup, self-hosting

## Action Items

**Paige Ruppel**
Provide exact timeline details regarding the full LaunchDarkly to Growth Book migration completion (15:48)
Continue engaging with Growth Book resources and community for implementing advanced statistical methods and improve analytics event standardization (07:45)

**Elyse Fox**
Send Paige up-to-date documentation, blog posts, and API resources concerning Growth Book’s stale flag management and removal tooling improvements (14:20)
Relay Paige’s feedback regarding SDK standardization and runtime observability to Growth Book technical team (18:40)
Facilitate connection between Paige and Chris from customer success for training and experimentation outreach programs (25:10)
Share information about Growth Book’s AI assistant and embedded best practice skills to support experiment design and analysis (28:15)

# LaunchDarkly migration & GrowthBook experience - ShiftKey
Date: 2026-08-26 | Duration: 40m

## Summary
The team successfully completed a swift migration from LaunchDarkly to Growth Book by the end of June, influenced by contract expiration and efforts to consolidate tools across business units. Although the initial focus was on feature flag parity, advanced experimentation capabilities are anticipated as maturity increases. Current practices involve manual, rule-based flagging, with ambitions to adopt automated rollouts and experimentation techniques in the future. The integration of a data warehouse is crucial for steering decisions and enhancing analytics, with ongoing needs for training and enablement identified. The organization operates separate Growth Book instances due to data privacy considerations, affecting their feature flag management and product metrics.

feature flags, migration, experimentation, product analytics, platform consolidation, data warehouse
